gen-gf-turret-road-gf-lunasima: Round, bold, and bent like a loop of tubing. Lunasima follows in a modern sans-serif whose c tips never creep toward touching, so the loud heading gets a quiet partner.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-lxgw-marker-gothic: Big round shapes with a pen-drawn line, no brush swell anywhere. And LXGW Marker Gothic, in sans-serif form, brings a wide c like a bracelet pulled apart and a gentle dip in its thin strokes.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-m-plus-1: M PLUS 1 gives every e and a a big open eye, drawn with the flat line of a fineliner. Turret Road's bold heading sits above it comfortably.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-m-plus-1p: Turret Road looks bent from a single wire, bold and commanding. M PLUS 1p, a sans-serif with openness at every curve end, is the lighter counterweight that makes the pair work.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-m-plus-2: Approachable and businesslike, with a gaping c and one fixed nib width, the body text speaks plainly. M PLUS 2 handles quiet reading, while Turret Road, round as open parentheses, does the shouting.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-m-plus-code-latin: Rounded forms like open parentheses, drawn with a pen-like line that never changes weight, define the commanding Turret Road. M PLUS Code Latin handles the reading, its pitcher-mouth c staying friendly.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: M PLUS Rounded 1c ends its terminals short of curling back in, a soft sans-serif foil to the heading. Turret Road's rod-stock lines are what make the pair stand out.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-manjari: Turret Road arrives bold and commanding, its round forms like open parentheses. Manjari, a sans-serif with wide, unclosed terminals and a steady line weight, is what makes the pair approachable.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-meera-inimai: Meera Inimai has open-ended curves with room to breathe, and a blueprint-lettering feel of constant line. But Turret Road, bold and commanding above it, supplies the loud voice that this plain sans leaves out.
